title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): $E$ is an extension $0\to\Omega\to E\to\mathcal O_S\to 0$ of locally free modules, given by an $\Omega$-torsor $T$ with class $c\in H^1(S,\Omega)$. $P$ is the associated projective bundle, with the section $\sigma$ defined by the quotient $E\to\mathcal O$. $\hat S$ is the structure sheaf of the formal completion $\hat P$ of $P$ along $\sigma$. The previous page shows that $\hat S$ is the twist of the completed symmetric algebra $\mathrm{Sym}^\wedge(\Omega)$ by $T$. The twist uses the action of $\Omega$ by the 'projective translations' $u_a$, which fix the section and act trivially on the tangent space; on homogeneous elements of degree $n$ this is $g\mapsto g/(1+a)^n$. In affine coordinates this is the Möbius-type map $x\mapsto x/(1+\langle a,x\rangle)$.

This page draws the consequences.

(1) Let $\hat J$ be the augmentation ideal, i.e. the ideal of the section. The $u_a$ act trivially on $\mathrm{gr}^1$, so $\mathrm{gr}^1_{\hat J}\hat S\simeq\Omega$. Hence $\mathrm{gr}^\bullet_{\hat J}\hat S\simeq\mathrm{Sym}^\bullet\Omega$: the twist is invisible on the associated graded.

(2) The first nontrivial information sits in the two-step quotients $\hat J^n/\hat J^{n+2}$. Each is an extension of $\mathrm{gr}^n=\mathrm{Sym}^n\Omega$ by $\mathrm{gr}^{n+1}=\mathrm{Sym}^{n+1}\Omega$. On the untwisted model, $u_a$ sends $f+g$ ($\deg f=n$, $\deg g=n+1$) to
$$f/(1+a)^n+g/(1+a)^{n+1}\equiv f-naf+g \pmod{\hat J^{n+2}}.$$
So $u_a$ induces the automorphism of the split extension given by $-n\,v_n(a)$. Here
$$v_n:\Omega\to\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}(\mathrm{Sym}^n\Omega,\mathrm{Sym}^{n+1}\Omega),\qquad v_n(a)(f)=af,$$
and the target is the sheaf of automorphisms of the extension that are trivial on both graded pieces.

(3) Twisting by $T$ therefore gives the following. The torsor of the extension $\hat J^n/\hat J^{n+2}$ is the pushout of $T$ along $-n v_n$. Its class is $c'=(-n v_n)_*(c)$ in $H^1(\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}(\mathrm{Sym}^n\Omega,\mathrm{Sym}^{n+1}\Omega))$; this is the boxed 'classe $c\times_\Omega[\ldots,-nv_n]$'. The parenthetical remark says $v_n$ is an isomorphism when $\Omega$ is invertible. In that case $\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}(\Omega^{\otimes n},\Omega^{\otimes n+1})=\Omega$, so $-nv_n$ is an isomorphism once $n$ is invertible (always for $n=1$). The class $c$ can then be recovered from the second-order structure.

Purpose: this is used on the next page. An $n$-projective connection on a smooth $X/S$ is defined as an isomorphism between the $n$-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of the diagonal ($P^n_{X/S}$) and that of the section of such a $P$. For $n=1$ this forces $\Omega\simeq\Omega^1_{X/S}$. For $n=2$, the page's computation with $n=1$ forces the class of the principal-parts extension $0\to\mathrm{Sym}^2\Omega^1\to P^2/\ldots\to\Omega^1\to 0$ to equal $(-v_1)_*(c)$. This is an obstruction-type compatibility linking $E$ with the Atiyah-type class of $X$ (for curves, $c$ is essentially forced, as in the theory of indigenous bundles / opers).
errors: Sign: $f/(1+a)^n\equiv f-naf$, not $f+naf$. Either the transcription misreads a minus sign or the manuscript has a slip. The subsequent use of $-nv_n$ is consistent with the minus sign.

The parenthetical condition is stated loosely ('car. ≠ …'). $v_n$ is an iso exactly when $\Omega$ is invertible; $-nv_n$ is an iso iff in addition $n$ is invertible on $S$. For $n=1$ there is no characteristic restriction.

Gap: the computation is done on the split model and then transported by twisting. This is legitimate, but it implicitly uses that the $\Omega$-action preserves the $\hat J$-adic filtration and acts trivially on the graded pieces. That is true and checked on the previous page.

ideas.what: Formal neighbourhood of the canonical section of the projective bundle of an extension E of O by Ω, described as a twist of the completed symmetric algebra by an Ω-torsor through 'projective translations' g ↦ g/(1+a)^deg
ideas.modern_name: formal neighbourhood of a section / twisted completed symmetric algebra; affine-to-projective transition (Möbius) group
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (deformation to the normal cone; Abate–Bracci–Tovena; Camacho–Movasati on neighbourhoods of submanifolds)

ideas.what: Class of the two-step extension J^n/J^{n+2} equals the pushout of the torsor class along -n v_n, v_n(a)(f)=af
ideas.modern_name: first-order obstruction / linearization class of a formal neighbourhood (Grauert/Griffiths-type obstruction classes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grauert (1962), Griffiths (1966) for analytic neighbourhoods; Abate–Bracci–Tovena

ideas.what: Use of this to compare with principal parts P^2_{X/S} in defining n-projective connections (next page)
ideas.modern_name: projective structures as Cartan geometries / opers / indigenous bundles; Atiyah-class compatibility

missed.claim: An algebraic, characteristic-sensitive treatment of projective structures of order n. A projective structure is an iso of infinitesimal neighbourhoods of the diagonal with those of a section of a P(E), with explicit extension classes $(-n v_n)_*(c)$ recording when E is determined (Ω invertible, n invertible). This is in the spirit of later Cartan-geometry/oper formulations but predates them in this precise form; a minor unpublished detail rather than a new theorem.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The factor n shows where characteristic p intervenes (n ≡ 0 mod p), which relates to Mochizuki's p-adic uniformization and dormant opers. It is mostly of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but routine computation of the graded pieces and second-order extension classes of the formal neighbourhood of a section of a projective bundle. It is interesting only as part of Grothendieck's algebraic definition of projective connections, whose general idea is known from later literature.
transcription_corrections: 'f + naf + g' should likely read 'f − naf + g' (consistent with $f/(1+a)^n$ and with the later $-n v_n$).
First lines: likely 'Conséquence : Si $\hat J$ est l'idéal d'augmentation de $\hat S$, filtration $\hat J$-adique, on a …'.
'$J^n/J^{n+2}$' should be '$\hat J^n/\hat J^{n+2}$'; 'Aut d'ext de $\hat J^{(a)n}/\hat J^{(a)n+2}$' refers to automorphisms of the extension trivial on graded pieces.
'(Si car. ≠ … n'est un iso si Ω inversible)' probably reads roughly '(c'est un iso si Ω inversible)', with a characteristic caveat on n.
